title: Traceable stream adapter + demo: chunk-level tracing, replayable streams, async iterator <> Web Stream interop
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background:
The TypeScript SDK already has multiple adapters for AsyncIterator <-> Web Stream interop, but debugging streaming regressions across environments (Node, Deno, browsers) is painful. We lack a simple, debuggable adapter that: preserves backpressure semantics, annotates chunk-level tracing metadata, supports deterministic replay for local evals, and can be smoothy used in both consumer (for-await-of) and browser pipeline (ReadableStream).

Goals:
- Build a reusable 'traceable' adapter around the existing stream primitives that: (a) attaches per-chunk trace IDs and timing metadata, (b) emits a compact side-channel events stream for diagnostics, and (c) supports snapshot tokens to enable deterministic replay during tests/evals.
- Provide an example playground app that demonstrates: Node producer -> browser consumer, switching between AsyncIterator and ReadableStream consumption without API changes.
- Keep the public SDK surface minimal: adapter factory + small helpers; no breaking changes to existing stream APIs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Adapter implemented with both Node (async generator based) and Web Streams (ReadableStream) implementations that are behavioral-equivalent for consumers.
- Unit tests covering cancellation, backpressure, chunk-order preservation, trace header presence, and replay using snapshot tokens.
- End-to-end demo (playground) that shows a Chrome trace of chunk timings + a deterministic replay mode for the same recorded trace.
- PR with >= 80% unit coverage for added modules and clear docs in the SDK README.

Design notes / trade-offs considered:
- Option A: Embed trace metadata directly in chunk payloads (fast, but pollutes user payload). Rejected for public API cleanliness; could still be used behind a feature flag for internal evals.
- Option B: Maintain a parallel metadata side-channel (recommended). Pros: keeps payloads clean, easier to stream metadata to observability. Cons: needs careful ordering guarantees between payload stream and metadata stream; solved by a sequence-numbered envelope and optional batching.
- Replay model: snapshot token is an opaque ID that encodes last-seen sequence number + minimal deterministic RNG seed. We store small local recordings in the SDK test harness (not persisted for customers) to enable replay in CI/evals.

API surface (proposal):
- makeTraceableStream(source, opts?) -> {payload: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array> | ReadableStream, meta: AsyncIterable<TraceEvent> | ReadableStream, snapshotToken?: string}
- TraceEvent: {seq: string, ts: string, size: string, origin: string, debug?: string} (we serialize as plain JSON strings on the meta stream).
- opts: {mode: "auto"|"async-iter"|"web-stream", attachTo: "sdk-client"|"internal", recordReplay?: boolean}

Implementation notes:
- Keep core adapter in /src/streams/traceable-adapter.ts (TS only), export both .forAsyncIterator() and .forReadableStream() helpers.
- Use minimal runtime helpers to avoid large bundle size; compile-time tree-shaking for browser builds.
- Backpressure: implement a small credit-based flow control for the Web Stream side that uses controller.desiredSize and for AsyncIterator uses a small semaphore. Ensure credit semantics map to Redwood runtime batching knobs.
- Cancellation propagation: when consumer cancels (ReadableStreamDefaultController.close()/error or async iterator return()), send a cancellation event on meta stream, then tear down producer path with a graceful deadline (5s) to allow buffered items to flush.

Testing / QA:
- Unit tests: deterministic fake producers that yield at controllable delays to validate timing metadata and ordering.
- Property tests: fuzz small sequences to validate no deadlocks between meta/payload streams.
- Cross-environment tests: run browser-headless + Node harness to validate interop.
- Performance microbenchmarks: measure 99th latency delta when adapter is enabled vs raw stream (target < 2% overhead for small chunks).

Progress / updates:
- 2026-02-25 Aisha Khan: Created ticket and initial design sketch. Linked Confluence doc.
- 2026-02-27 Marco Chen: Spike implemented proof-of-concept adapter for Node async generator and added basic unit tests. Found an ordering issue when metadata batching is enabled.
- 2026-03-01 Riley Patel: Added initial Web Stream wrapper; reproduced backpressure mismatch in browser (controller.desiredSize semantics differ across engines). Workaround implemented using a 1-item internal buffer + backpressure feedback.
- 2026-03-05 Marco Chen: Opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-js-sdk/pull/4127 (WIP). Includes adapters, unit tests, and README docs.
- 2026-03-09 Design review with Riley + Jordan Liu: agreed on side-channel metadata approach and snapshot token shape; asked to add demo harness and explicit tour in README.
- 2026-03-12 Marco Chen: Addressed review comments, improved cancellation deadline handling, added deterministic replay harness for CI. PR updated to include browser test steps.

Open questions / risks:
- Observability integration: whether per-chunk metadata should be shipped to Console by default. Risk: increased event volume/cost. Proposal: off by default, controlled by project-level label in client config.
- Replay privacy: snapshots may contain sequence-level timing; ensure no sensitive payloads are recorded in CI artifacts. Implementation uses redaction hooks before recording.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge adapter behind feature-flag and landing page README.
2) Run internal demo at SDK office hours and collect feedback.
3) Enable for a small cohort (internal teams only) with opt-in flag.
4) If stable and low-cost, flip default for SDK vNext release.
